messages.content:
You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: The verifications of the IGEA devices are entrusted to an authorised body: under the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011, for how long at least must the authorised body keep the documents relating to the verification activity?

Passages:
[0] eu-reg-2024-1689, Art. 18(1) — rank: law
Article 18 Documentation keeping. 1. The provider shall, for a period ending 10 years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service, keep at the disposal of the national competent authorities: (a) the technical documentation referred to in Article 11; (b) the documentation concerning the quality management system referred to in Article 17; (c) the documentation concerning the changes approved by notified bodies, where applicable; (d) the decisions and other documents issued by the notified bodies, where applicable; (e) the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47.

[1] eu-dir-2014-68, Annex III, 4 — rank: law
4. Verification of conformity by examination and testing of every item of pressure equipment 4.1. In particular, the notified body shall: — verify that the personnel undertaking the permanent joining of parts and the non-destructive tests are qualified or approved in accordance with points 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 of Annex I, — verify the certificate issued by the materials manufacturer in accordance with point 4.3 of Annex I, — carry out or have carried out the final inspection and proof test referred to in point 3.2 of Annex I and examine the safety devices, if applicable. 4.2. The manufacturer shall keep the certificates of conformity available for inspection by the national authorities for 10 years after the pressure equipment has been placed on the market.

[2] REG, Art. 11(3) — rank: law
Article 11 Obligations of manufacturers of partly completed machinery. 3. Manufacturers shall keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of incorporation at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years after the partly completed machinery has been placed on the market. Where relevant, the source code or the programming logic included in the technical documentation shall, upon a reasoned request, be made available to the competent national authorities, if that source code or programming logic is necessary in order for them to be able to check compliance with the relevant essential health and safety requirements set out in Annex III.

[3] eu-reg-2023-988, Art. 11(6) — rank: law
Article 11 Obligations of importers. 6. Importers shall keep the copy of technical documentation referred to in Article 9(2) at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities for a period of 10 years after they have placed the product on the market and shall ensure that the documents referred to in Article 9(2), as applicable, can be made available to those authorities, upon request.

[4] eu-dir-2014-34, Annex V, 4 — rank: law
4. Verification of conformity by examination and testing of every product 4.1. In the absence of such a harmonised standard, the notified body concerned shall decide on the appropriate tests to be carried out. 4.2. The manufacturer shall keep the certificates of conformity available for inspection by the national authorities for 10 years after the product has been placed on the market.

[5] eu-dir-2014-34, Annex IX, 4 — rank: law
4. Verification A notified body chosen by the manufacturer shall carry out appropriate examinations and tests, set out in the relevant harmonised standards and/or equivalent tests set out in other relevant technical specifications, to check the conformity of the product with the applicable requirements of this Directive, or have them carried out. In the absence of such a harmonised standard the notified body concerned shall decide on the appropriate tests to be carried out. The notified body shall issue a certificate of conformity in respect of the examinations and tests carried out and shall affix its identification number to the approved product, or have it affixed under its responsibility. The manufacturer shall keep the certificates of conformity at the disposal of the national authorities for 10 years after the product has been placed on the market.

[6] igea-equipment, p. 5 — rank: plant record
4. manuale di installazione, uso e manutenzione (solo apparecchi a marchio CE); 5. se superiore a 20 anni di età, certificazione di verifica strutturale dei cicli di vita residui; 4. IMPEGNI AGGIUDICATARIO / VERIFICATORE L’aggiudicatario si impegna a:  rispettare quanto contenuto nella presente Scheda Tecnica;  rispettare le disposizioni in materia di salute e sicurezza contenute nel Decreto Legislativo 81/08;  rispettare le disposizioni del D.lgs. 81/08 e nel D.M. 11 aprile 2011 riguardo la disciplina delle modalità di effettuazione delle verifiche periodiche di cui all’All. VII del decreto legislativo 9 aprile 2008 n° 81;  Effettuare le verifiche periodiche richieste entro le scadenze;  Pianificare i controlli, congiuntamente agli incaricati IGEA, dei diversi apparecchi dando comunicazione a IGEA con un preavviso di almeno 15 giorni – tempo necessario per la programmazione relativa ai punti 4.1 – 4.2 (impegni Appaltatore);  Rilasciare il verbale di verifica;  Comunicare il nominativo del verificatore incaricato; . 5

[7] eu-dir-2014-33, Annex XI, 4 — rank: law
4. Surveillance under the responsibility of the notified body 4.1. 4.2. (a) the quality system documentation; (b) the quality records provided for in the design part of the quality system, such as results of analyses, calculations, tests; (c) the quality records provided for in the part of the quality system concerning acceptance of supplies and installation, such as inspection reports and test data, calibration data, reports on the qualifications of the personnel concerned. 4.3. 4.4. 5. The installer shall, keep at the disposal of the national authorities for a period ending 10 years after the lift has been placed on the market: (a) the documentation referred to in point 3.1(c); (b) the technical documentation referred to in point 3.1(d); (c) the information relating to the changes referred to in the second paragraph of point 3.5; (d) the decisions and reports from the notified body which are referred to in the fourth paragraph of point 3.5 and in points 4.3 and 4.4. 6. Each notified body shall inform its notifying authority of full quality system approval decision(s) issued or withdrawn, and shall, periodically or upon request, make available to its notifying authority the list of approval decisions refused, suspended or otherwise restricted. Each notified body shall inform the other notified bodies of quality system approval decision(s) which it has refused, suspended or withdrawn, and, upon request, of approval decisions which it has issued. The notified body shall keep a copy of the approval decision issued, its annexes and additions, as well as the technical documentation for 15 years from the date of their issue. On request, the notified body shall provide the Commission and the Member States with a copy of quality system approval decision(s) issued.

[8] eu-dir-2014-33, Annex XII, 4 — rank: law
4. Surveillance under the responsibility of the notified body 4.1. 4.2. (a) the quality system documentation; (b) the technical documentation; (c) the quality records, such as inspection reports and test data, calibration data, reports on the qualifications of the personnel concerned. 4.3. 4.4. 5. The installer shall, keep at the disposal of the national authorities for a period ending 10 years after the lift has been placed on the market: (a) the documentation referred to in point 3.1(c); (b) the technical documentation referred to in point 3.1(d); (c) the information relating to the changes referred to in point 3.4.1; (d) the decisions and reports from the notified body which are referred to in the second paragraph of point 3.4.2, and in points 4.3 and 4.4. 6. Each notified body shall inform its notifying authority of quality system approval decision(s) issued or withdrawn, and shall, periodically or upon request, make available to its notifying authority the list of approval decisions refused, suspended or otherwise restricted. Each notified body shall inform the other notified bodies of quality system approval decision(s) which it has refused, suspended or withdrawn, and, upon request, of approval decision(s) which it has issued. On request, the notified body shall provide the Commission and the Member States with a copy of quality system approval decision(s) issued.

[9] eu-reg-2023-988, Art. 11(11) — rank: law
Article 11 Obligations of importers. 11. The register of complaints shall only store those personal data that are necessary for the importer to investigate the complaint about an alleged dangerous product. Such data shall only be kept for as long as is necessary for the purposes of the investigation and in any event no longer than five years after the data have been entered.

[10] eu-reg-2024-1689, Art. 33(4) — rank: law
Article 33 Subsidiaries of notified bodies and subcontracting. 4. The relevant documents concerning the assessment of the qualifications of the subcontractor or the subsidiary and the work carried out by them under this Regulation shall be kept at the disposal of the notifying authority for a period of five years from the termination date of the subcontracting.

[11] eu-dir-2014-68, Annex III, 4 — rank: law
4. Verification A notified body chosen by the manufacturer shall carry out appropriate examinations and tests, set out in the relevant harmonised standard(s) and/or equivalent tests, to check the conformity of the pressure equipment with the applicable requirements of this Directive, or have them carried out. In the absence of such a harmonised standard the notified body concerned shall decide on the appropriate tests to be carried out applying other technical specifications. In particular the notified body shall: — examine the technical documentation with respect to the design and the manufacturing procedures, — assess the materials used where these are not in conformity with the relevant harmonised standards or with a European approval for pressure equipment materials, and check the certificate issued by the material manufacturer in accordance with point 4.3 of Annex I, — approve the procedures for the permanent joining of parts or check that they have been previously approved in accordance with point 3.1.2 of Annex I, — verify the qualifications or approvals required under points 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 of Annex I, — carry out the final inspection referred to in point 3.2.1 of Annex I, perform or have performed the proof test referred to in point 3.2.2 of Annex I, and examine the safety devices, if applicable. The notified body shall issue a certificate of conformity in respect of the examinations and tests carried out and shall affix its identification number to the approved pressure equipment, or have it affixed under its responsibility. The manufacturer shall keep the certificates of conformity at the disposal of the national authorities for 10 years after the pressure equipment has been placed on the market.

{"reasoning": "The question asks for the minimum retention period set by the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 for documents kept by an authorised verification body. Passage 6 (plant record) says the contractor must comply with the D.M. 11 aprile 2011 on how periodic verifications are carried out, but it gives no retention period. The other passages cover EU directives and regulations with different subjects and periods (10 years, 5 years, 15 years), so none of them answer the question for this decree. The answer is unknown.",

"text": "The passages do not state how long the authorised body must keep verification documents under the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011. The IGEA equipment technical sheet (plant record, p. 5) only refers to that decree for the rules on how periodic verifications are carried out.",
"evidence": [{"passage": 6, "quote": "rispettare le disposizioni del D.lgs. 81/08 e nel D.M. 11 aprile 2011 riguardo la disciplina delle modalità di effettuazione delle verifiche periodiche di cui all’All. VII del decreto legislativo 9 aprile 2008 n° 81;"}]}
